_readme: Every parameter: lo = conservative (fewer riders / smaller market), base, hi = aggressive. tag: FACT (public, verified, cited in research/03-market-size.md), ESTIMATE (derived from several sources), ASSUMPTION (no direct evidence; replace with HMP data or field tests). Sources are abbreviated; full citations in research/03-market-size.md and research/raw/market/. Change log 2026-09-06: M5 (DoorDash two-wheel miles) removed from the two-wheel blend after an SF back-test showed the miles->courier conversion overstates SF 3x; kept as a labelled sanity output. M4 rebuilt on a per-rider basis (HMP share of SF two-wheel weekly-active people) instead of per-restaurant. 2026-09-06 v2 after LA-reality review: DoorDash 49% haircut for declared-mode misreporting; mode-specific weekly/daily for two-wheelers; standing e-scooter bucket split out; gas share raised; zone intensity, reach, penetration and maturity lowered; robot displacement added; SOM route B rebuilt on customers per daily-active two-wheel courier. v3 after methodology review: orders_per_courier_day derived from deliveries/week and weekly->daily (one free parameter, not two); M1 and M2 are acknowledged as ONE orders route (M1's LA/NYC intensity ratio is built from M2's inputs) cross-checked against M3 (supply) only; M5 rebuilt as an NYC-transfer of DoorDash two-wheel miles (sanity range, not blended); delivery_share_of_app_workers restricted to de-duplicated restaurant couriers; doordash_us_share on an all-vertical basis.

restaurants_target_zone.note: LA County DPH Restaurant & Market Inventory (2026-07), restaurant program elements deduped to facilities, point-in-polygon: Downtown LA NC + Arts District/Little Tokyo NC 910, Wilshire Center-Koreatown NC 611, Westlake N+S NC 104, Pico Union NC 126, Empowerment Congress North (USC) 211

restaurants_radius_3mi.note: same source, 3-mile circle around 768 Ceres (34.0363, -118.2447); circle is 91% City of LA; Vernon (own health dept) missing

restaurants_city_la.note: same source, union of 99 Neighborhood Council polygons

restaurants_county_la.note: same source, all LA County (excl. Pasadena, Long Beach, Vernon which run own health departments)

restaurants_sf_core.note: SF DPH inspections 2024-present (tvy3-wexg), RESTAURANT/TAKE-OUT/FAST FOOD permits, SoMa+Mission+Tenderloin+FiDi/South Beach analysis neighborhoods

nyc_weekly_active_couriers.note: NYC DCWP Nov 2022: 61,000 working in any given week (Q2 2022); Mayor 2024-07: 'more than 60,000'; NYSERDA Dec 2025: 'over 65,000'

nyc_deliveries_per_courier_week.note: DCWP: 124M deliveries/yr (2021-22) / 52 / 61,000 = 39; Q4 2024: 2.72M deliveries/wk / 60k trip-performing accounts = 45 (accounts not deduped)

la_orders_per_restaurant_vs_nyc.note: NYC ~0.33 deliveries/resident/week (2.77M/wk / 8.48M) vs US average ~0.11 (DoorDash 'over 3M/day' US 2024 / ~0.62 share / 340M). LA assumed 1.2-1.8x US average -> 0.4-0.6 of NYC per capita; restaurants per capita similar in both (2.7 vs 2.9 per 1,000). Also consistent with DoorDash two-wheel miles LA 38.3M vs NYC 45.2M at 49% vs 55% shares (city label boundary undefined)

la_deliveries_per_courier_week.note: deliveries per weekly-active courier (people). Anchors: DoorDash US 8M annual Dashers x ~10/52 weeks active = ~1.5M weekly-active; 3.6M deliveries/day x 7 / 1.5M = 16.4 per weekly-active Dasher-week; Seattle 12.7 offers/account-week; NYC career couriers 39-45. lo = higher productivity = fewer couriers

weekly_to_daily_active.note: blended daily/weekly for all couriers (car-dominated). DoorDash: ~4 hrs/wk in 2-3 hr sessions -> 0.2-0.35; NYC full-timers ~0.85; DoorDash-consistent pair with 16.4 deliveries/wk and ~7 orders/day is 0.33. orders_per_courier_day is DERIVED = deliveries_per_courier_week / (7 x this)

zone_order_intensity_vs_county.note: app orders per DPH restaurant in the zone vs county: DTLA DPH count includes arena/convention/hotel/Grand Central Market stalls/mission kitchens (+32% vs NAICS 7225) and DTLA office occupancy is ~half of 2019 (CBRE Q3 2025 vacancy 33%); offsets: Koreatown late-night, USC students, orders exported to Silver Lake/Mid-City

doordash_us_deliveries_per_day.note: DoorDash Dash Report 2025 (2024 data): 'over 3 million deliveries per day' US; FY2025 global Total Orders 3,172M (+23%, ex-Deliveroo +20% in Q4) -> 2025 US 3.3-4.0M/day

doordash_us_share.note: DoorDash's share of ALL US app deliveries (its 3.6M/day numerator includes grocery/DashMart). Second Measure Mar 2024: 67% of meal-delivery SALES; all-vertical share ~60%; 2025-26 aggregators 56-61%. lo = higher share = smaller total market

la_county_share_us_orders.note: LA County 9.76M / US 340.1M = 2.87% population share x intensity 1.0 / 1.2 / 1.45 (DoorDash: 'Greater Los Angeles' is its highest-volume metro; warm climate; but car-based)

ca_app_based_workers_quarter_active.note: UC Riverside CEFD Feb 2022: 800,000 CA drivers completed >=1 ride/delivery in Q3 2021 across DoorDash+Instacart+Lyft+Uber (two-thirds <5 hrs/wk); Flex/Public First: 870,000 'active' CA app workers (2022). Grown modestly to 2025

la_county_share_ca_gig.note: LA County = 24.85% of CA population (DOF 2026), 26.6% of CA NAICS 722 employment (QCEW Jun 2025), 26.2% of CA NAICS 492 nonemployer couriers (Census 2023: 44,977 of 171,603)

delivery_share_of_app_workers.note: share of quarter-active CA app-worker REGISTRATIONS that are restaurant couriers after de-duplicating multi-platform registrations (UCR: 800k 'may include duplicate drivers across platforms'; Flex: 1.9 platforms per worker; Berkeley: 45% multi-app) and excluding rideshare-only, Instacart and Amazon Flex

quarterly_to_weekly_active.note: NYC DCWP: 61,000 weekly / 122,104 quarterly-unique = 0.50; Seattle OLS: ~13.7k weekly unique / 34,646 quarterly = ~0.40; DoorDash: typical Dasher active ~10 of 52 weeks, 73% dash <4 weeks per quarter -> ~0.25-0.30

la_two_wheel_delivery_share.note: DoorDash 2026 Two-Wheeled Progress Report: Los Angeles, CA 49% of deliveries on two wheels (2025; FACT for DoorDash's DECLARED dash type). Haircut for (a) car couriers running 'bike' mode to catch short high-paying orders (DoorDash policy explicitly threatens deactivation for mode misreporting; TikTok how-tos exist) and (b) Uber Eats/Grubhub LA being more car-heavy (scooter mode <50cc only). lo 0.35 = 25% misreporting + Uber blend; hi 0.49 = DoorDash figure taken at face value

two_wheel_delivery_to_courier_share.note: two-wheel couriers do more deliveries per hour and more hours per active day, so courier share < delivery share. NYC DCWP: non-car 56% of workers vs 78% of deliveries (0.72), 69% of hours (0.89). For daily-active the factor sits between the hours and workers ratios

zone_two_wheel_uplift.note: dense core vs LA-wide. Critic's restaurant-weighted sub-zone view: DTLA ~50% two-wheel couriers, Koreatown ~35% (KBBQ pickups car-dominated), Westlake/Pico-Union ~45%, USC ~30% -> ~42% zone courier share. No neighborhood data exists

ebike_emoped_share_of_two_wheel.note: e-bikes incl. e-moto (Surron/Talaria/Super73) and e-mopeds (NIU/Segway/HMP-class), EXCLUDING standing e-scooters. NYC intercept 2025: 79% electric incl. 24% rental e-bikes (no LA equivalent). LA pushes gas up (Uber <50cc rule, $899 Keeway 50, lane-splitting legal, walk-up housing without charging) and electric toward standing scooters and sub-$1,200 fat-tire e-bikes

gas_scooter_share_of_two_wheel.note: gas 49-150cc scooters and motorcycles; NYC 13% gas moped; LA drivers: Uber Eats scooter mode, $899-2,795 used 50-150cc (Craigslist LA 2026-09-06), Latin American moto-delivery culture, DTLA 'Honda Ruckus delivery setup' videos. lo = more gas = fewer HMP-type riders

two_wheel_serviceable_share.note: share of two-wheel couriers HMP could sell or rent to (e-bike riders as upgrade/rental, gas riders as conversion, pedal riders as upgrade); excludes riders on employer/rental fleets, kids' bikes, walking

car_convertible_share.note: share of car couriers in the zone who would switch to two wheels within 24 months; critics: 2-8% realistic vs 20-30% implied; DoorDash Chicago/Whizz program converted 'more than 150' car Dashers city-wide

reachable_share_768ceres.note: share of zone two-wheel riders who would use 768 Ceres: road miles 7th/Figueroa 1.5, Little Tokyo <1, Westlake 2.8, USC 2.7, Wilshire/Western 4.5 (31% of zone restaurants); no walk-in frontage; Skid Row edge after dark. Mitigant: the site sits on the inbound path from Boyle Heights / Lincoln Heights / South Central where DTLA two-wheel couriers live

penetration_m12.note: share of SAM paying by month 12. Priors: Zoomo retreated from LA to NYC-only; Whizz skipped LA; DoorDash+Whizz Chicago converted 'more than 150' car Dashers in ~9 months citywide; SF reached 600-1,000 vehicles in ~25 months WITH founder on site, walk-in and seeded referrals

penetration_m24.note: by month 24; hi = SF-like dynamics replicate

hmp_sf_active_customers.note: HMP: >1,000 vehicles sold, 300+ battery subscribers, ~100 on rent; Gazetteer SF 2026-04-02: 'over 600 e-mopeds in SF, targeting 1,000 by year-end'. Active = vehicles in regular use. Retagged ESTIMATE after SF back-test: cumulative sales include non-SF, commuters, retired units; verified recurring-paying count is ~400 (300+ battery + ~100 rental)

sf_two_wheel_courier_share.note: SF 72% of DoorDash deliveries on two wheels (2025) x delivery-to-courier factor 0.75-0.9. lo = higher SF share = LA looks relatively smaller

la_maturity_vs_sf_at_m24.note: LA hub at month 24 vs SF store at ~25 months: no founder on site, no seeded network, Spanish/Korean-speaking communities, no walk-in, Skid Row edge

la_two_wheel_miles_per_day_doordash.note: DoorDash 2026 Two-Wheeled Progress Report p.7: Los Angeles, CA 38,304,846 two-wheel miles in a two-month 2025 window (/61 days). SF 21,413,128 (351k/day); NYC 45,238,991 (742k/day)

county_share_of_doordash_label_miles.note: DoorDash does not define 'Los Angeles, CA'. The same table lists Santa Clara, Sunnyvale, Oakland and San Jose separately, so labels are sub-metro; if the label is the City of LA, the county holds ~1.5x the label's miles; if metro, ~0.75x. On-app miles per two-wheel delivery come out ~11-12 for both NYC and LA under the county reading, favouring 1.0

zone_residual_reach_vs_sf.note: SF penetration already embeds SF's spatial decay (all SF restaurants within 5 mi of 261 6th St, 77% within 3 mi). The LA zone stretches 4-6 mi to Koreatown/USC and the hub sits on the zone's east edge next to Skid Row, so a residual discount applies; la_maturity_vs_sf_at_m24 carries the no-founder/no-walk-in handicap separately

standing_escooter_share_of_two_wheel.note: standing e-scooters (Levy partner shops in 90010/90006; Amazon-grade). Not an e-moped customer in the same way. lo = more standing scooters

two_wheel_weekly_to_daily.note: mode-specific daily/weekly for two-wheel couriers: they bought a vehicle for the job and work 5-6 days (NYC non-car 22.2 hrs/wk; NYC full-timers 6+ days -> ~0.85). lo = higher ratio = fewer distinct people

robot_displacement_m24.note: sidewalk robots (Coco >1,000 robots incl. DTLA/Koreatown/USC, targeting 10,000; Serve on DoorDash/Uber Eats/Grubhub) take the sub-1.5-mile orders bike-mode couriers depend on; factor on zone two-wheel demand at M24

hmp_sf_customers_per_two_wheel_daily.note: HMP active SF customers (600-1,000; press 600+ e-mopeds on SF streets Apr 2026) / SF daily-active two-wheel couriers from the same model run on SF (M1-M3: ~2,160; scenario 0.8k-5.1k). 800/2,160 = 0.37. Ratio of people to daily-actives, so it does not depend on the weekly/daily ratio. lo = lower penetration

nyc_two_wheel_miles_per_day_doordash.note: DoorDash 2026 report p.7: New York, NY 45,238,991 two-wheel miles / 61 days

doordash_share_nyc.note: DoorDash share of NYC app deliveries: McKinsey via DCWP 2022 ~25-28%; DoorDash has gained share nationally since. lo = smaller DoorDash NYC base -> smaller LA transfer

nyc_two_wheel_delivery_share_doordash.note: DoorDash 2026 report: New York 55% of deliveries on two wheels

doordash_share_of_two_wheel_couriers_la.note: DoorDash's share of LA two-wheel couriers: above its ~60% order share because Uber Eats LA caps scooter mode at <50cc and skews to cars. lo = higher share = fewer total
